---
title: 'Publish to TestFlight and the App Store'
status: implemented
description: 'Upload signed iOS builds to App Store Connect and follow them through TestFlight, review and phased release.'
---

A build can upload its signed IPA to App Store Connect when it ends. Oore
then sends the build to TestFlight groups or attaches it to an App Store
version, and records each step as a release. Set it up in the pipeline, as
below, and with a `.oore.yaml` version 2 file choose the destination and the
signing identity per workflow; see [Publish per workflow](#publish-per-workflow).

All App Store Connect calls leave from the Direct macOS runner and the daemon
host. Allow outbound HTTPS to `api.appstoreconnect.apple.com` and Apple's
upload hosts.

## What you need

- App developer, maintainer, instance admin, or instance owner access.
- iOS signing with an App Store Connect API key, as in
  [Configure App Store Connect signing](/build/sign/ios/app-store-connect).
- The app already exists in App Store Connect with the pipeline's bundle ID.
- For TestFlight, the names of the groups to distribute to.

## 1. Export for the App Store

1. Open the pipeline and select **Edit**.
2. Under **Signing > iOS**, set **Distribution** to **App Store**.
3. Select **Save changes**.

- In API or Hybrid mode, saving discards the stored profiles and syncs App
  Store distribution profiles from App Store Connect.
- In Manual mode, upload an App Store distribution profile for each bundle
  ID. Oore rejects ad hoc or development profiles for this distribution.

Ad hoc and App Store profiles are not interchangeable, which is why changing
the distribution replaces them. App Store IPAs cannot be installed from Oore.
Testers install them through TestFlight.

## 2. Turn on publishing

1. Open the pipeline's **Publishing** tab.
2. Under **App Store Connect**, check that the readiness list shows
   **App Store distribution** and **App Store Connect API key** as ready.
3. Turn on **Upload to App Store Connect after each successful build**.
4. For **Destination**, choose **TestFlight** or **App Store**.
   - For TestFlight, enter the **TestFlight groups**.
   - For the App Store, turn on **Submit for review** to submit the version
     once the build is attached. Then **Phased release** turns on Apple's
     seven-day phased release, and **Replace an open submission** lets Oore
     cancel another open App Review submission for the app first. Apple
     allows one per app; with this off, the release is blocked until you
     cancel the other one.
   - **Release after approval** chooses **When approved**, **When I release
     it** (press **Release now** on the release) or **On a date**, with the
     date and time.
5. Under **Release notes**, add **What to Test** or **What's New** text per
   locale. **Notes from the repository** names a folder with one
   `<locale>.txt` file, or fastlane's `<locale>/release_notes.txt`, per
   language; those files replace the typed notes for their locales. Notes
   written in **What's new in this release** when a build starts replace the
   first locale's notes for that build (see
   [Notes for one release](#notes-for-one-release)).
6. Under **Export compliance**, turn on **Uses non-exempt encryption** only if
   the app uses encryption beyond what iOS provides, such as HTTPS.
7. Select **Turn on App Store publishing**, or **Save changes** when
   publishing was already on.

For automation, set `"export_method": "app_store"` with
`PUT /v1/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/ios-signing`, then send the publish settings
with `PUT /v1/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/publish/app-store`:

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "destination": "testflight",
  "testflight_groups": ["Internal QA"],
  "release_notes": [{ "locale": "en-US", "whats_new": "Checkout fixes" }],
  "uses_non_exempt_encryption": false
}
```

For an App Store release, set `"destination": "app_store"`, then
`submit_for_review`, `phased_release`, `release_type` (`after_approval`,
`manual` or `scheduled`), `earliest_release_date` and
`cancel_previous_submission` as needed. `release_notes_dir` and `preflight`
apply to both destinations.

## Notes for one release

The Run build drawer shows **Ready to submit?** and **What's new in this
release** for a pipeline or workflow that uploads to a store. The checklist
lists what Apple or Google would refuse, such as unanswered age rating
questions, each with a link to the page that fixes it, so it shows before a
long build. The pipeline's overview shows the same list, and
[`oore pipeline readiness`](/reference/cli/oore-pipeline-readiness) prints
it.

The notes field starts empty, which keeps the pipeline's notes. **Draft from
commits** fills it with the commit titles since the last build, and **Same
as #N** copies the last notes written for the pipeline. Typed notes replace
the App Store's first locale (or add `en-US`) and Google Play's notes for
this build only; a re-run keeps them. `oore build run --notes` does the same
from the command line.

## TestFlight groups per workflow

To send one workflow's builds to other testers, open the pipeline's
**Workflows** tab, select the workflow, and list the groups under
**TestFlight groups**. They replace the groups the file and the pipeline's
settings name, for uploads to TestFlight only.

Oore warns on Home two weeks before the newest TestFlight build of a group
reaches Apple's 90 day limit, and again in its last three days, so testers
are not left without the app.

## What happens after a build

1. The runner uploads the IPA with `xcrun altool` and the pipeline's API key.
   The key is written to a private folder only for the upload.
2. The release starts in **processing** while Apple processes the build.
   Oore sets the export compliance answer once the build is valid.
3. **TestFlight:** Oore adds the build to the groups and sets "What to Test".
   Internal groups complete at once. External groups go to beta review
   (**in review**) and complete when Apple approves.
4. **App Store:** Oore finds or creates the version, attaches the build, sets
   "What's New" and, if asked, submits it (**in review**). When the version is
   live the release follows the phased release (**rolling** at 1, 2, 5, 10,
   20, 50 and 100 percent) until it is **complete**.

Pause, resume and complete on the release change Apple's phased release.
Apple sets the percentages, so raising a step is not available.

## Pre-flight

Before the upload, the **Publishing** tab and the runner check what Apple
would otherwise refuse after the upload:

- the API key reaches App Store Connect and the app exists for the bundle ID;
- the age rating and App Review contact details are filled in;
- no other review submission is open, unless **Replace an open submission**
  is on;
- the app icon has no transparency;
- anything Apple refused on an earlier submission of this app, until a later
  submission goes through.

**Pre-flight checks** decides what a failure does. **Automatic** stops the
upload once the app has had a release in review or live, and only warns
before that. **Stop the upload** and **Warn only** fix the choice, and
**Off** skips the checks. The same levels apply to Google Play, where Oore
validates the edit before committing it. Read the checks from the API with
`GET /v1/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/publish/readiness`.

## Release states

A release shows where it is in the store, and what you need to do when the
store is waiting on you:

| State          | Meaning                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Processing** | Apple is processing the upload.                                                                                                         |
| **Blocked**    | The store refused a step, or the version is ready but nobody submitted it. The release names the reason and links to App Store Connect. |
| **In review**  | App Review or TestFlight beta review has the version.                                                                                   |
| **Approved**   | App Review approved it and it waits for its release time, or for **Release now**.                                                       |
| **Rejected**   | App Review rejected it. Read why in the Resolution Center, fix it, then **Resubmit for review**.                                        |
| **Rolling**    | Live, with a phased release in progress.                                                                                                |
| **Complete**   | Live for everyone, or added to the TestFlight groups.                                                                                   |

A blocked release says what is wrong in one sentence when Oore knows the
refusal (age rating, "What's New", App Review contact details, export
compliance, App Privacy, agreements, screenshots, a build number already
used), with a button to the App Store Connect page that fixes it. The
store's own text is under **Details from the store**. A release in review
says how long reviews usually take for the app, from its last five reviews.

A rejected release shows the reviewer's message and the guidelines it
names, with **Reply in App Store Connect** and **Resubmit with a new build**,
which opens Run build for the same pipeline, branch and workflow.

A store refusal blocks the release at once and notifies once per reason
(`release_blocked`). A network or server error blocks it only after an hour
of failures. A blocked release leaves the state on its own once the store
accepts the next check; **Check again now** checks at once.

The release menu offers what the store allows next: **Release now**,
**Resubmit for review**, **Pull from review** and **Check again now**.
Releases Oore was already following are read again with these states, and the
release history notes the first change. Failed releases stay failed.

When the same version waits as **Approved** in both stores, the app's
**Releases** tab offers **Release both** under **Versions**, which releases
each one now.

## Releases made outside Oore

Every 15 minutes, and when you select **Check stores** on Home, Oore reads
the App Store versions and Google Play tracks of every app a pipeline
publishes. A release it did not make shows on Home and the Releases page
marked **Found in store**, with no build, and on its own release page with
when Oore found it and its version code. Oore follows it like its own, but
never schedules rollout steps for a Play release it found; **Manage rollout
with Oore** on the release attaches a schedule.

## Verify the result

- The build shows a succeeded **Upload to App Store Connect** step (`publish-app-store`).
- The build's **Release** tab shows the release moving through
  **Processing** to **Complete** for internal TestFlight groups, or to
  **In review** for external groups and App Store submissions.
- App Store Connect shows the build in the TestFlight groups, or attached to
  the App Store version.

## Publish per workflow

With a `.oore.yaml` version 2 file, an ad hoc test workflow and an App Store
release workflow can run from one pipeline:

```yaml
workflows:
  adhoc:
    signing: { ios: coin-adhoc } # ad hoc profiles; publishes nowhere
  release:
    signing: { ios: coin-app-store } # App Store profiles
    targets:
      ios:
        build: flutter build ipa --release
        publish:
          app_store: { destination: testflight, groups: [Internal QA] }
```

- `signing.ios` names an iOS distribution identity in the
  [app's signing library](/build/sign/project-library). Its certificate
  and profiles replace the pipeline's for that workflow, and the export
  follows its profiles. A workflow that uploads to App Store Connect needs an
  identity with App Store profiles; an ad hoc one refuses the build with
  `invalid_signing`.
- `publish.app_store` sets the destination, groups, `submit_for_review` and
  `phased_release`, in place of the **Publishing** tab's.
- The upload still uses the pipeline's App Store Connect API key, so keep the
  pipeline's iOS signing on with **Distribution** set to **App Store**, and
  App Store Connect publishing turned on as in
  [step 2](#2-turn-on-publishing). Release notes and the export compliance
  answer also come from the **Publishing** tab.
- To stop one workflow's uploads without a commit, open the pipeline's
  **Workflows** tab, select **Settings** on the workflow, and turn
  **Publishing** off. **iOS signing** there can pick another identity.

`oore pipeline validate --project "$PROJECT_ID"` checks the identity names
before you push, and `oore pipeline plan` prints each workflow's identity,
destination and export. Every field is in
[Publish](/reference/config/oore-yaml-v2#publish) and
[Signing](/reference/config/oore-yaml-v2#signing).

## Store health on Home

After the first release, the daemon reads the app's hang rate and launch time
per version from App Store Connect power and performance metrics, using the
App Store Connect key of the pipeline that made the newest release. Home shows
the latest version's numbers for a typical user on all iPhones. They refresh
every six hours, and Apple only reports them once enough users have run a
version.

## Troubleshooting

**The Upload to App Store Connect step fails**

Fix the cause, such as an expired API key, then
[retry the upload](/build/run/retry-step). The stored IPA is uploaded again
without rebuilding or re-signing.

**The release fails with "has no app with bundle ID"**

Create the app in App Store Connect with the same bundle ID, then rebuild.

**The upload fails with a bundle version error**

Each upload needs a higher build number than the last one for that version.
Pass `--build-number` to `flutter build ipa`.

**"What's New" is not set**

Apple does not accept "What's New" on an app's first version. The release
history notes the skipped field and the release continues.
